title: Extraction of nuclei from archived post-mortem tissues for single-nucleus sequencing applications
protocol: Cut 30-50 mg of frozen tissue per sample using a scalpel.
Keep the cut tissue on dry ice while cutting to minimize degradation.
Transfer the tissue to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube using a spatula and return it to dry ice.
Clean the scalpel and spatula with 70% ethanol between samples.
Use a fresh weigh boat for each sample.
Transfer tissue from the microcentrifuge tube to a douncing tube on ice using a spatula.
Add 3 mL of ice-cold lysis buffer to the tissue in the douncing tube.
Dounce the tissue with a loose pestle 10 times and 5 more times with a tight pestle.
Transfer the homogenized tissue to a 15 mL centrifuge tube by pouring.
Add 2 mL of chilled lysis buffer to the transferred homogenized tissue.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes, gently swirling to mix 2 times during incubation.
Add 5 ml of chilled wash buffer to lysed tissue to quench lysis. Swirl to mix.
Place a 30 μm MACs SmartStrainer on a 15 mL centrifuge tube. Pipette the lysed tissue suspension on top of the filter to remove cell debris and large clumps. Tap the filter gently if flow is blocked.
In the precooled Allegra-14X centrifuge, spin down the lysed tissue suspensions at 500g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Decant supernatant into a waste beaker without disrupting the nuclei pellet.
Using a 10 mL serological pipette, add 10 mL of nuclei wash buffer to the pelleted nuclei and gently pipet 8-10 times to mix.
Repeat step 5-7 using the resuspended nuclei.
Using a 10 mL serological pipette, add 5 mL of nuclei wash buffer to the pelleted nuclei and gently pipet 8-10 times to mix.
Repeat steps for resuspended nuclei.
Add 1 mL of nuclei wash buffer to pelleted nuclei and gently pipette 8-10 times to mix.
Mix 1 mL of 50% working solution of Optiprep™ with nuclei suspension to make 2 mL of 25% iodixanol solution containing nuclei.
Prepare an Optiprep™ cushion of 2 ml of 29% Optiprep™ solution in a 5ml Eppendorf centrifuge tube.
Gently add the 2ml nuclei suspension on top of the Optiprep™ cushion by pipetting slowly against the wall of the tube to avoid mixing.
Spin the tubes containing nuclei layered over Optiprep™ cushion at 10,000g for 30 minutes at 4°C in a precooled Eppendorf centrifuge.
Carefully pour out the supernatant leaving the least amount of volume without disrupting the pellet.
Resuspend nuclei pellets in 500 μL or less of nuclei wash buffer and gently pipette 8-10 times to resuspend.
Dilute human neurons' nuclei to around 500,000 cells/mL or 500 cells/μL using nuclei wash buffer.
Add Hoechst stain to the resuspended nuclei at a 1:2000 dilution.
Filter 200 μl of the sample through a 40 μm Flowmi pipette tip filter before counting and loading (optional).
Load 10 μl of sample onto a disposable hemocytometer slide.
Mix the full volume of the nuclei suspension several times before loading for accurate counts.
Set the Evos to 10X magnification and image the entire hemocytometer grid field of view in DAPI and bright field.
Make the RT Master Mix according to the Chromium protocol CG00052 Rev. D or later.
Aliquot appropriate volumes of master mix and water into PCR tubes based on the number of nuclei for capture.
Resuspend nuclei by pipette mixing the full volume several times immediately before loading to prevent aggregation of nuclei.
Load the Chromium Chip and harvest the nuclei captured in droplet according to the Chromium protocol CG00052 Rev. D.
Perform reverse transcription, cDNA amplification, and library preparation according to the Chromium protocol CG00052 Rev. D.
Sequence libraries on an Illumina sequencer.
Sequencing two samples per lane of a HiSeq 4000 machine can yield ~100,000 reads per nucleus based on default CellRanger parameters.
Use downstream analysis options for the sequencing results as described in Box 1.
Build a pre-mRNA reference using the cellranger mkref command with refdata-cellranger-GRCh38-1.2.0 transcriptome for human nuclei experiments.
Demultiplex reads by sample index using the cellranger mkfastq command.
Load unfiltered gene barcode matrices for each sample into R using the Read10X function.
Create Seurat objects corresponding to each sample using the CreateSeuratObject function with the imported unfiltered gene-barcode matrices provided as the raw data.
Combine individual Seurat objects for each sample sequentially using the MergeSeurat function.
Remove all mitochondrial genes from the dataset.
Exclude genes not detected in any cell.
